proposed_assumptions.condition: For every \(K\), \(c\in\mathcal C\), and \(1\le f\le L\), conditional on the training sample outside \(\mathcal V_{cf}\), the path \(u\mapsto R_{cf}(u\mid X_{ci})\) is of bounded variation on \([0,\max_{1\le\ell\le d_c}t_{c\ell}]\) for \(P_c\)-almost every \(X_{ci}\), almost surely over the training sample.
proposed_assumptions.reason: The Stieltjes integrator in the exact conditional-bias identity is \(dR_{cf}\). Survival-ratio consistency in the frozen event metric does not imply that this signed measure has finite variation; an explicit oscillatory-hazard sequence shows the omission can create bias of order \(a_K\).
proposed_assumptions.not_crux: This condition does not assert a small score remainder or asymptotic linearity; it restricts the path regularity of the primitive fitted event-survival ratio. It is nevertheless a load-bearing, substantive learner-class restriction.

proposed_assumptions.condition:
The foldwise relative-survival variations satisfy
\[
\max_{c\in\mathcal C}\max_{1\le f\le L}\max_{1\le\ell\le d_c}
\left\|V_{cf\ell}(X_{ci})\right\|_{L_2(P_c)}=O_P(a_K).
\]
proposed_assumptions.reason: Cauchy--Schwarz bounds the conditional score bias by the product of the inverse-censor error norm and \(\|V_{cf\ell}(X)\|_2\). Matching the latter to \(a_K\) is therefore the substantive learner restriction that yields the advertised \(O_P(a_Kb_K)\) remainder.
proposed_assumptions.not_crux: This condition bounds a primitive total-variation norm and does not assume the score bias, empirical-process remainder, or target expansion. The proof must still derive the product bound from the exact Stieltjes identity and Cauchy--Schwarz.

proposed_core_edits.name: R_{cf}

proposed.name: R_{cf}
proposed.space: real-valued paths on the fixed cell horizon
proposed.def: For \(c\in\mathcal C\) and fold \(f\), define \[R_{cf}(u\mid x)=\frac{Q_c(u\mid x)}{\widehat Q_{c,-f}(u\mid x)}-1,\] using the existing convention \(0/0=1\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The repair must expose the relative-survival path that is the signed Stieltjes integrator in the exact score remainder.

proposed_core_edits.name: V_{cf\ell}

proposed.name: V_{cf\ell}
proposed.space: extended nonnegative real-valued functions of the covariate
proposed.def: For \(c\in\mathcal C\), fold \(f\), and \(1\le\ell\le d_c\), define \[V_{cf\ell}(x)=|dR_{cf}(\mathord\cdot\mid x)|((0,t_{c\ell}]),\] the total variation of the relative-survival path on the coordinate horizon, with value \(+\infty\) when the path is not of bounded variation.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The learner restriction is stated on the total variation actually appearing in the Cauchy--Schwarz remainder bound.

proposed.statement:
For every fixed cell and all its fixed coordinates jointly, the estimator in Definition~\ref{def:cell-estimator} satisfies
\[
\sqrt K(\widehat s_c-s_c)=K^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^K\phi_c(O_{ci})+o_P(1).
\]
The conditional second-order remainder is \(O_P(a_Kb_K)+o_P(K^{-1/2})\), no first-order event- or censor-nuisance term remains, and the foldwise plug-in influence vectors are \(L_2(P_c)\)-consistent. Stacking over the finite set \(\mathcal C\) gives the same expansion for \((\widehat y,\widehat M,\widehat B,\widehat s_1)\) with influence \(\Phi_i\).
proposed.justification: This is the load-bearing orthogonality result: without its explicit Stieltjes variation control, the spectral delta method can propagate a first-order censoring bias.
proposed.gap: The frozen event-ratio and inverse-censor metrics do not control the total variation of the relative-survival path. The exact remainder is a Stieltjes product, so the joint panel expansion requires the separately disclosed bounded-variation and variation-rate restrictions.
proposed.consumer: The lemma supplies censoring-robust cell inputs for every country and treatment-line block in Han and Shah's 925-patient TCL panel.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The exact proof spine uses origin support, learner normalization, bounded variation of \(R_{cf}\), and the \(L_2(P_c)\) variation rate. These premises belong only on the cell expansion, so spectral and inference results inherit them transitively.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The target cannot be marked proved until the proposed bounded-variation and relative-survival variation-rate assumptions are adjudicated and installed in its dependency spine.
open_obligations.obstruction: Under the present frozen assumptions, survival-ratio and inverse-censor errors can both be \(O(\varepsilon_K)\) while oscillating at frequency \(\varepsilon_K^{-1}\), making the exact Stieltjes remainder of order \(\varepsilon_K\), rather than \(\varepsilon_K^2\). With \(\varepsilon_K=K^{-1/3}\), the frozen product-rate condition holds but root-\(K\) asymptotic linearity fails.
open_obligations.attempted: The score mean, product-integral quotient identity, Cauchy--Schwarz variation bound, cross-fitted conditional Chebyshev step, joint finite-cell stacking, and plug-in influence consistency were derived. The only unavailable premises are precisely the two proposed learner-path restrictions; no first-order nuisance term remains after they are imposed.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The following calculation proves the target conditional on Assumptions~\ref{ass:event-origin-support}, \ref{ass:learner-origin-normalization}, \ref{ass:relative-survival-bv}, and \ref{ass:relative-survival-variation-rate}; the last two assumptions are proposed in this round and therefore are not silently treated as frozen premises.

Fix \(c\in\mathcal C\), \(1\le \ell\le d_c\), and a fold \(f\), and abbreviate \(t=t_{c\ell}\), \(Q=Q_c\), \(G=G_c\), \(\bar Q=\widehat Q_{c,-f}\), and \(\bar G=\widehat G_{c,-f}\).  Let \(\mathcal T_{cf}\) be the training-sample sigma-field.  Assumption~\ref{ass:event-origin-support} gives \(Q(0\mid X)=1\), and Assumption~\ref{ass:learner-origin-normalization} gives \(\bar Q(0\mid X)=1\).  All statements below concerning \(\bar Q\) and \(\bar G\) are conditional on \(\mathcal T_{cf}\).

Put
\[
N(u)=\mathbf 1\{U\le u,\Delta=1\},
\qquad
Y(u)=\mathbf 1\{U\ge u\}.
\]
By Assumption~\ref{ass:conditional-censoring}, the definition \(\Delta=\mathbf 1\{T\le C\}\), and the left-continuous convention \(G(u\mid X)=P(C\ge u\mid X)\),
\[
E\{dN(u)\mid X\}=Q(u-\mid X)G(u\mid X)\Lambda(du\mid X),
\qquad
E\{Y(u)\mid X\}=Q(u-\mid X)G(u\mid X).
\]
The absence of an event atom at zero, supplied by Assumption~\ref{ass:event-origin-support}, makes the integration interval \((0,t]\) agree with Definition~\ref{def:aipcw-score}.  Taking the conditional expectation of that definition and applying Tonelli separately to the positive and negative finite hazard integrals yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
E\{\psi_t(O;\bar Q,\bar G)\mid X,\mathcal T_{cf}\}
&=\bar Q(t\mid X)\left[
1+\int_{(0,t]}
\frac{Q(u-\mid X)G(u\mid X)}{\bar Q(u\mid X)\bar G(u\mid X)}
(\bar\Lambda-\Lambda)(du\mid X)
\right].
\end{aligned}
\]
Here and below, the displayed integral with respect to \(\bar\Lambda-\Lambda\) denotes the difference of the two finite Stieltjes integrals with the same predictable integrand.

Define \(R(u\mid X)=Q(u\mid X)/\bar Q(u\mid X)-1\), using the declared \(0/0=1\) convention.  The product-integral quotient rule gives
\[
dR(u\mid X)=
\frac{Q(u-\mid X)}{\bar Q(u\mid X)}
(\bar\Lambda-\Lambda)(du\mid X).
\]
For completeness, at a jump \(u\), the product-integral equations \(Q(u)=Q(u-)\{1-\Delta\Lambda(u)\}\) and \(\bar Q(u)=\bar Q(u-)\{1-\Delta\bar\Lambda(u)\}\) imply
\[
\Delta\!\left(\frac Q{\bar Q}\right)(u)
=\frac{Q(u-)}{\bar Q(u)}
\{\Delta\bar\Lambda(u)-\Delta\Lambda(u)\};
\]
on the continuous part the ordinary quotient rule gives the same signed differential.  Because \(R(0\mid X)=0\), integration from zero to \(t\) gives
\[
Q(t\mid X)=\bar Q(t\mid X)\left[
1+\int_{(0,t]}
\frac{Q(u-\mid X)}{\bar Q(u\mid X)}
(\bar\Lambda-\Lambda)(du\mid X)
\right].
\]
Subtracting this identity from the preceding score mean proves the exact orthogonality identity
\[
\mathfrak R_{cf\ell}(X)
:=E\{\psi_t(O;\bar Q,\bar G)\mid X,\mathcal T_{cf}\}-Q(t\mid X)
=\bar Q(t\mid X)
\int_{(0,t]}
\left\{\frac{G(u\mid X)}{\bar G(u\mid X)}-1\right\}
dR(u\mid X).
\]
In particular, setting either nuisance equal to its truth makes the right-hand side zero, so there is no first-order event- or censor-nuisance term.

Let
\[
A_{cf\ell}(X)=
\sup_{0\le u\le t}
\left|\frac1{\bar G(u\mid X)}-\frac1{G(u\mid X)}\right|.
\]
Since \(0\le \bar Q(t\mid X)\le1\), \(0\le G(u\mid X)\le1\), and Assumption~\ref{ass:relative-survival-bv} makes \(dR\) a finite signed Stieltjes measure,
\[
\begin{aligned}
|\mathfrak R_{cf\ell}(X)|
&\le A_{cf\ell}(X)
|dR(\cdot\mid X)|((0,t])\\
&=A_{cf\ell}(X)V_{cf\ell}(X).
\end{aligned}
\]
Assumption~\ref{ass:censor-estimability} gives \(\|A_{cf\ell}\|_{L_2(P_c)}=O_P(b_K)\), while Assumption~\ref{ass:relative-survival-variation-rate} gives \(\|V_{cf\ell}\|_{L_2(P_c)}=O_P(a_K)\).  Cauchy--Schwarz, conditional on \(\mathcal T_{cf}\), therefore yields the required second-order bound
\[
\left|P_c\{\psi_t(\bar Q,\bar G)-\psi_t(Q,G)\}\right|
\le \|A_{cf\ell}\|_{L_2(P_c)}
\|V_{cf\ell}\|_{L_2(P_c)}
=O_P(a_Kb_K).
\]
This is the load-bearing use of the proposed variation-rate assumption.  Assumption~\ref{ass:nuisance-product-rate} turns the last quantity into \(o_P(K^{-1/2})\).

We next control the cross-fitted empirical term.  For \(0\le u\le t\), put
\[
r_t(u\mid X)=\frac{Q(t\mid X)}{Q(u\mid X)},
\qquad
\bar r_t(u\mid X)=\frac{\bar Q(t\mid X)}{\bar Q(u\mid X)},
\]
again using \(0/0=1\).  These paths are nondecreasing in \(u\) and take values in \([0,1]\).  The same jump calculation as above gives
\[
d\bar r_t(u\mid X)=\bar r_t(u\mid X)\bar\Lambda(du\mid X).
\]
Consequently Definition~\ref{def:aipcw-score} can be rewritten, for \(w=t\wedge U\), as
\[
\psi_t(O;\bar Q,\bar G)
=\bar Q(t\mid X)
-\mathbf 1\{U\le t,\Delta=1\}
\frac{\bar r_t(U\mid X)}{\bar G(U\mid X)}
+\int_{(0,w]}\frac1{\bar G(u\mid X)}\,d\bar r_t(u\mid X).
\]
Define
\[
D_{Q,cf\ell}(X)=
\sup_{0\le u\le t}|\bar r_t(u\mid X)-r_t(u\mid X)|.
\]
Assumption~\ref{ass:event-estimability} gives \(\|D_{Q,cf\ell}\|_{L_2(P_c)}=O_P(a_K)\), and \(0\le D_{Q,cf\ell}\le1\).  Assumption~\ref{ass:censor-positivity} makes \(G^{-1}\) nondecreasing with supremum at most \(g^{-1}\).  Splitting the last Stieltjes integral as
\[
\int\frac1{\bar G}\,d\bar r_t-
\int\frac1G\,dr_t
=\int\left(\frac1{\bar G}-\frac1G\right)d\bar r_t
+\int\frac1G\,d(\bar r_t-r_t)
\]
and applying Stieltjes integration by parts to the second term gives a constant \(C_g<\infty\), depending only on \(g\), such that
\[
\left|
\int_{(0,w]}\frac1{\bar G}\,d\bar r_t-
\int_{(0,w]}\frac1G\,dr_t
\right|
\le A_{cf\ell}(X)+C_gD_{Q,cf\ell}(X).
\]
Indeed, the first term is bounded by \(A_{cf\ell}\) because the total variation of the nondecreasing path \(\bar r_t\) is at most one; the boundary terms and the integral against \(d(G^{-1})\) in the second term are bounded by a constant times \(D_{Q,cf\ell}\), because \(G^{-1}\) has total variation at most \(g^{-1}-1\).  The baseline and event terms in the rewritten score satisfy the same bound.  Hence
\[
\|\psi_t(\bar Q,\bar G)-\psi_t(Q,G)\|_{L_2(P_c)}
\le C_g\{
\|D_{Q,cf\ell}\|_{L_2(P_c)}+
\|A_{cf\ell}\|_{L_2(P_c)}\}
=O_P(a_K+b_K)=o_P(1),
\]
where the last equality uses Assumptions~\ref{ass:event-rate-vanishes} and \ref{ass:censor-rate-vanishes}.

Let \(n_{cf}=|\mathcal V_{cf}|\), let \(\mathbb P_{cf}\) be the empirical measure on that validation fold, and abbreviate the fitted and true scores by \(\widehat\psi_{cf\ell}\) and \(\psi_{c\ell}\).  Since the folds partition the \(K\) observations, Definition~\ref{def:cell-estimator} and \(P_c\psi_{c\ell}=S_c(t)\) give the exact decomposition
\[
\begin{aligned}
\widehat s_{c\ell}-S_c(t)
&=K^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^K\phi_{c\ell}(O_{ci})\\
&\quad+\sum_{f=1}^L\frac{n_{cf}}K
(\mathbb P_{cf}-P_c)
(\widehat\psi_{cf\ell}-\psi_{c\ell})\\
&\quad+\sum_{f=1}^L\frac{n_{cf}}K
P_c(\widehat\psi_{cf\ell}-\psi_{c\ell}).
\end{aligned}
\]
By Assumption~\ref{ass:cell-iid}, validation observations are independent of \(\mathcal T_{cf}\) and are conditionally i.i.d. with law \(P_c\).  Conditional Chebyshev and the preceding \(L_2(P_c)\) convergence therefore imply
\[
(\mathbb P_{cf}-P_c)
(\widehat\psi_{cf\ell}-\psi_{c\ell})
=o_P(n_{cf}^{-1/2})=o_P(K^{-1/2}),
\]
because \(L\) is fixed and the folds are approximately equal by Assumption~\ref{ass:fixed-panel}.  The bias term in the exact decomposition is \(O_P(a_Kb_K)=o_P(K^{-1/2})\) by the Cauchy--Schwarz bound above.  It follows that
\[
\sqrt K\{\widehat s_{c\ell}-S_c(t)\}
=K^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^K\phi_{c\ell}(O_{ci})+o_P(1).
\]

The number of folds, cells, and coordinates is fixed by Assumption~\ref{ass:fixed-panel}.  A finite union bound therefore makes every displayed rate simultaneous over \(c\), \(f\), and \(\ell\).  Assumption~\ref{ass:cross-cell-independence} then permits the cell influences with common within-cell index \(i\) to be stacked as \(\Phi_i\), and extracting the target-pre, donor-pre, donor-post, and factual-post blocks gives the asserted joint expansion for \((\widehat y,\widehat M,\widehat B,\widehat s_1)\).

Finally define the foldwise centered plug-in influence coordinate by
\[
\widehat\phi_{cf\ell}(O)=
\widehat\psi_{cf\ell}(O)-\widehat s_{c\ell}.
\]
Assumption~\ref{ass:influence-moment} supplies finite second moments, so the empirical average of the true influence is \(O_P(K^{-1/2})\).  The expansion just proved gives \(|\widehat s_{c\ell}-S_c(t)|=o_P(1)\); hence
\[
\|\widehat\phi_{cf\ell}-\phi_{c\ell}\|_{L_2(P_c)}
\le
\|\widehat\psi_{cf\ell}-\psi_{c\ell}\|_{L_2(P_c)}
+|\widehat s_{c\ell}-S_c(t)|
=o_P(1).
\]
Another finite union bound proves joint \(L_2(P_c)\)-consistency of all plug-in influence vectors.  Thus every conclusion of the target follows once the four explicitly named support, normalization, bounded-variation, and variation-rate premises are part of its frozen dependency spine.

prose_updates.tldr: The augmented-IPCW cell score has an exact orthogonality identity, but the usual event-ratio and inverse-censor convergence rates alone do not deliver the claimed product remainder. The missing quantity is the total variation of the foldwise relative-survival path \(R_{cf}\). Under event-origin support, learner normalization, bounded variation, and the substantive rate \(\max_{c,f,\ell}\|V_{cf\ell}(X)\|_2=O_P(a_K)\), Cauchy--Schwarz gives the required \(O_P(a_Kb_K)\) cell bias and supplies the repaired premise for spectral counterfactual and grid-RMST inference. Without that restriction, an oscillatory-hazard sequence violates root-\(K\) centering even though the frozen product-rate condition holds.

project_justification.gap: Synthetic Survival Control identifies a clinically relevant low-rank counterfactual but assumes non-informative censoring and provides no influence-function limit law. Existing orthogonal survival-score rates do not by themselves control the Stieltjes variation that appears when those scores feed a learned panel map.
project_justification.niche: With fixed panel dimensions and many independent patients per cell, the cellwise survival problem is semiparametric, while the final counterfactual is a smooth multi-block spectral functional. The bridge requires both the complete pseudoinverse derivative and explicit path-variation control for the fitted event-survival ratio.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the exact augmented-IPCW Stieltjes remainder, exposes a necessary bounded-variation learner restriction and its \(L_2\) rate, and shows how the resulting joint cell influence vector feeds spectral, multiplier-band, and grid-RMST calculations. It also characterizes the unadjusted Kaplan--Meier/PCR probability limit and its fixed-bias region.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Fixed-fold cross-fitting estimates conditional event and censor survival. Besides \(a_K\to0\), \(b_K\to0\), and \(a_Kb_K=o(K^{-1/2})\), the event learner is normalized at the follow-up origin, its relative-survival error path \(R_{cf}\) is almost surely of bounded variation, and \(\max_{c,f,\ell}\|V_{cf\ell}(X)\|_{L_2(P_c)}=O_P(a_K)\). This variation condition is a substantive learner-class restriction, not a consequence of the ordinary product-rate assumption.

prose_updates.related_work: Han and Shah (2025) supply the low-rank survival-panel estimand, donor transport, and TCL application, but their Kaplan--Meier theory assumes non-informative censoring and points to IPCW as future work. Westling, Luedtke, Gilbert, and Carone (2024) supply the augmented survival-score architecture and single-law nuisance metrics, but those metrics alone do not control the total variation of the relative-survival Stieltjes integrator required here. Agarwal, Shah, and Shen (2025) clarify minimum-norm PCR and row-space transport without censoring-aware asymptotics. Golub and Pereyra (1973) provide the constant-rank pseudoinverse differential used as a technique ancestor. Curth, Poon, Nori, and Gonz\'alez (2024) motivate censoring-bias analysis in survival synthetic controls but do not derive this informative-censoring PCR pseudo-limit or its relatively open nonzero-bias region. Fan and Liao (2022) study factor-space recovery in growing panels, not the fixed-donor, weak-gap pseudoinverse problem considered here.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The positive theory is fixed-dimensional and, at the cell layer, applies only to event-survival learners whose relative-survival paths satisfy the stated bounded-variation and \(L_2\) variation-rate restrictions. Ordinary supremum or \(L_2\) consistency of survival ratios does not imply this property, so generic oscillatory learners are outside the theorem. The theory also does not cover a growing post grid, a shrinking singular gap, a selected rank, covariance degeneracy, or continuous-time RMST; the RMST target is exactly the fixed-grid functional \(q^\top(s_1-\theta)\).
prose_updates.honest_scope: The exact score identity shows that neither nuisance contributes a first-order term, while Cauchy--Schwarz supplies the product remainder only after the relative-survival variation rate is imposed. The joint-cell lemma therefore remains formally open until that substantive restriction is installed; the downstream spectral limit, multiplier band, and grid-RMST interval inherit it transitively. No variation or origin condition is imposed on the purely algebraic pseudoinverse differential or on the unadjusted Kaplan--Meier/PCR cancellation result. The weak-gap and rank-selection frontier remains an explicit open-ended question.

statement_notes.justification: This is the load-bearing orthogonality result: the spectral delta method is centered only when the exact Stieltjes nuisance remainder is \(o_P(K^{-1/2})\).
statement_notes.gap: The standard event-ratio and inverse-censor metrics leave the integrator's total variation uncontrolled. The repaired claim therefore discloses bounded variation and the rate \(\max_{c,f,\ell}\|V_{cf\ell}(X)\|_2=O_P(a_K)\) as substantive learner restrictions rather than treating them as part of a generic product-rate convention.
